subject: Archaeology
title: The Endurance: Shackleton's Ship Found
description: One-minute skill: The Endurance: Shackleton's Ship Found.

hook.text: Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance was crushed by Antarctic ice in 1915. It was found in 2022, perfectly preserved.

buildup.text: The ship sank in the Weddell Sea after being trapped in pack ice for months. Shackleton led all 27 men to safety.

discovery.text: A search team found it 10,000 feet deep using autonomous underwater vehicles.

twist.text: Cold Antarctic water and lack of wood-eating organisms preserved the ship almost perfectly — the masts still stand.

climax.text: The wreck is protected as a historic monument under the Antarctic Treaty. No artifacts may be removed.

punchline.text: The ice crushed it. The cold saved it. Endurance lived up to its name.

quiz.question: Why was the Endurance so well preserved after 107 years?
options: A thick layer of sediment quickly buried and sealed the wreck
Cold Antarctic water and the absence of wood-eating organisms preserved it
The ship's oak construction was naturally resistant to decay

details.summary: Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance, crushed by Antarctic ice in 1915, was found in 2022 at 3,008 meters in the Weddell Sea. Remarkably, the wooden ship was almost perfectly preserved in the frigid Antarctic water, with the name still legible on the stern
details.whyItMatters: Finding the Endurance after 107 years in the most hostile sea on Earth proved that advanced technology can locate any wreck. Its extraordinary preservation in Antarctic waters has opened new possibilities for deep polar archaeology.
takeaways: Endurance was found in 2022 at 3,008 meters in the Weddell Sea
The ship was almost perfectly preserved with the name still visible
It was a landmark achievement in deep polar exploration technology

faq.question: Why was the Endurance so well preserved?
faq.answer: The Weddell Sea's near-freezing temperatures, low light levels, and absence of wood-eating organisms like shipworm created near-perfect preservation conditions. The ship sat upright on the seafloor with masts intact, looking almost exactly as it did when it sank in 1915.

faq.question: Will artifacts be recovered from the Endurance?
faq.answer: No. The wreck is protected as an Antarctic Historic Site and Monument under international treaty. The team documented it extensively using underwater drones and photogrammetry but did not touch or disturb the site. It will remain on the seafloor as a protected monument.
